segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinegrower.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Every branch in me that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every branch that does bear fruit he prunes clean so that it may bear more fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Remain in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever remains in me, and I in them, bears much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever does not remain in me is thrown out like a branch and withers; such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire and burned.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you remain in me and my words remain in you, ask for whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: In this my Father is glorified: that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you. Remain in my love.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father’s commandments and remain in his love.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I have spoken these things to you so that my joy may be in you and your joy may be made full.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This is my commandment: that you love one another as I have loved you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one has greater love than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You are my friends if you do what I command you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I no longer call you slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing. I have called you friends, because everything I heard from my Father I have made known to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that remains, so that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: These things I command you so that you will love one another.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “If the world hates you, know that it has hated me before it hated you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for that reason the world hates you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Remember the word that I spoke to you: ‘A slave is not greater than his master.’ If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they kept my word, they will keep yours too.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But they will do all these things to you on account of my name, because they do not know the one who sent me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever hates me hates my Father also.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If I had not done among them the works that no one else has done, they would have no sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But this is so that the word written in their law may be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without cause.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who comes forth from the Father, he will testify about me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And you also testify, because you have been with me from the beginning.

notes.note: In Israel’s Scriptures the vine or vineyard is a standing image for Israel itself, planted and tended by God and often rebuked for failing to bear good fruit (for example Psalm 80 and Isaiah 5). A first-century Jewish reader would hear Jesus’ claim to be the “true” vine against that background.

The verb can mean either “take away, remove” or “lift up.” Some interpreters argue that the vinegrower lifts fruitless branches off the ground so that they can bear. Most scholars take it as removal, which fits verse 6, and that reading is followed here.

The Greek verb means “to cleanse” and is here applied to clearing a vine. It is the verb behind the adjective “clean” in the next verse, and it also chimes in sound with “takes away” (airei / kathairei). “Prunes clean” keeps the link to verse 3 visible, which the plain “prunes” of most versions hides.

The traditional “abide” is now archaic and has a devotional colouring the Greek word lacks. It is the ordinary verb for staying or remaining somewhere, and it occurs eleven times in this chapter. “Remain” is used throughout, including for the fruit that “remains” in verse 16, so that the repetition can be heard.

notes.traditional: so shall ye be my disciples
notes.note: Manuscripts are divided between a subjunctive (“that you … become my disciples”) and a future (“and you will become my disciples”). The edition translated here reads the subjunctive. The sense is that bearing fruit is how they come to be, or show themselves to be, his disciples.

The Greek word denotes a slave, someone owned by a master, not a hired servant. The contrast with “friends” depends on this: a slave is given orders without explanations, while a friend is taken into confidence. Many recent versions still have “servants,” though “slaves” is widely acknowledged to be the more accurate sense.

The Greek form can be either a command (“know that”) or a statement (“you know that”). Most modern versions and commentators take it as a command, as here; the King James Version read it as a statement.

“Law” is used here in the broad sense of the Jewish Scriptures as a whole, since the words quoted come from the Psalms (see Psalms 35:19 and 69:4), not the five books of Moses. “Their law” means the Scriptures that the opponents themselves acknowledge.

Outside the New Testament the word is used of someone called in to speak on another’s behalf, and 1 John 2:1 clearly uses it that way of Jesus. That sense suits this verse, where the Advocate gives testimony. “Advocate,” “Helper” and “Counselor” are all in current use among translations; “Comforter” goes back to the older English versions.

The Greek form can be a statement (“you are testifying”) or a command (“you too must testify”), and translations differ. The present tense is kept here, and the English, like the Greek, can be read either way.
